_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false = must not load.

evals.prompt: At my day job (globex) we wrote a really good doc on retrying flaky webhook deliveries. I want the same lessons in my own open-source project acme-hooks. Copy it over and push it.
assertions: Writes a fresh generic version instead of copying the file as is, removing the employer's name, hosts, clients, internal ticket or decision-record ids and parity or 'inspired by' lines
Checks the commit author and committer email for the target repo before committing, and commits with the address the open-source repo expects rather than the employer address
Scans the diff and the commit metadata for employer markers before the push (scan_boundary.py with --range, or an equivalent grep over the diff and git log author/committer/message)
Keeps the employer markers out of any file in the target repo, including a patterns file or guard config

evals.prompt: An agent cloned my public repo into /tmp to make a quick fix and the commit it pushed shows my work email from my employer instead of my personal one. My ~/.gitconfig has an includeIf for ~/projects/personal/. Why, and how do I stop this from happening again?
assertions: Explains that includeIf gitdir only applies to repos under that directory, so a clone in /tmp falls back to the global identity
Recommends user.useConfigOnly = true with no global user.email so commits outside the scoped trees fail instead of guessing
For the already pushed commit, treats a history rewrite as a last resort with a plan (mirror backup, filter-repo --mailmap, tree-hash proof, forge purge) and mentions .mailmap as the low-cost option
Does not tell the user to force-push a rewrite immediately without a backup

evals.prompt: Check whether my employer's infra repo still mentions my own company acme anywhere. We cleaned it last week, but I want to be sure, including branches.
assertions: Keeps the list of acme markers in a patterns file outside the employer's repo, not in a file or CI variable of that repo
Searches for implicit references (phrases like the sibling estate, parity with, both clusters, org-qualified repo refs, hosts) and not only the name
Covers commit author and committer identities, commit messages, branch and tag names, and other branches without checking them out
Names the forge surfaces outside git (MR titles, descriptions and every note, issues, CI variables, registry names) as separate checks
Keeps the person's own name and work address and any functional image or chart paths rather than removing them

evals.prompt: In my side project the tracker MCP tools just created a task on my employer's board instead of my own. Both boards use a server called tracker. What happened?
assertions: Explains that a user-scope MCP server loads in every project, so the employer's tracker server was active in the side project
Recommends registering each organisation's server at local or project scope or through a per-project plugin, with distinct per-organisation names
Recommends confirming the tenant (an identity call or the server URL via claude mcp get) before any write

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md is 600 lines and Claude ignores half of it. Slim it down and make AGENTS.md the canonical file.
assertions: Does not load the org-boundaries skill

evals.prompt: Where should the API token for our deploy workflow live so the CI job can read it?
assertions: Does not load the org-boundaries skill
